messages:
alex: customer reported intermittent streaming failures when going through our customer's edge proxy (Fastly) — Go SDK client hits a parser error mid-stream and the connection drops. error seen: "json: invalid character '\\x00' after top-level value"

maria: thanks alex. can you paste the minimal repro and the go-sdk version? also any proxy config (chunk size, gzip, keepalive)

alex: reproducer steps below. go-sdk v0.9.7 (customer hasn't upgraded). repro: 1) start server that streams 5 JSON objects with small chunk sizes (simulate flush every 64 bytes) 2) route through fastly config w/ response_max_buffer 16384 3) client uses StreamDecoder from go-sdk and fails on object 3. curl through same proxy returns a clean concatenated stream and succeeds.

alex: small server code (golang):
```go
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)
for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
  fmt.Fprintf(w, `{\"id\": %d, \"t\": \"msg\"}` , i)
  flusher.Flush()
  time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
}
```

maria: hmm. that looks like chunk boundary fragmentation. do you see any NUL bytes (0x00) in the raw tcp captures or in the proxy logs? sometimes proxy does concat+pad for boundary alignment which can inject zeroes on some edge cases. also what's the exact go-sdk API call pattern? are you using the high-level Stream function or low-level scanner?

alex: we use the high-level Client.Stream(ctx, req) and then a for loop calling decoder.Scan() / decoder.NextJSON(&obj). repro log excerpt: 
```
decoder.Scan(): true
err = decoder.NextJSON(&ev) -> json: invalid character '\\x00' after top-level value
stream closed by remote: EOF
```

kevin: pinging @eng-runtime — could be our streaming scanner not tolerating padded chunks. recent changes to the scanner around v0.10.x tightened framing assumptions. the customer's sdk is old (0.9.7) but they see it only when proxying.

anya: quick mitigation for customers: 1) disable proxy response buffering/rewrites (Fastly: set response_max_buffer to 0 / streaming) 2) set Accept-Encoding: identity to avoid gzip+proxy recompose 3) upgrade go-sdk to v0.12.3 which includes a resync path and tolerant scanner. can you try 2 + upgrade?

alex: tried Accept-Encoding: identity — still hit the same error but it moved to object 4 instead of 3. disabling Fastly buffering made it succeed consistently. we need a long-term fix; customer wants SDK patch because they can't change edge config.

kevin: ok. we can patch the scanner to ignore NUL padding between top-level JSON values and resync. low risk. repo: github.com/redwood/go-sdk/stream/decoder. i'll open a PR with unit tests simulating padded chunks.

maria: escalation note for customer: suggest short-term workaround (disable buffering) + staged upgrade to patched sdk. request: customer logs (tcpdump) + full proxy config + exact HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 behaviour. i've asked them for pcap.

support-bot: created ticket SI-2026-1124 and linked to GH issue #784 (stream-decoder-nul-pad-resync).

alex: adding a small curl command we used to repro:
```
curl -v --http1.1 "https://edge.example.com/stream" -H "Accept-Encoding: identity" 
```

maria: thanks. please upload the pcap to the ticket. i'll coordinate with eng for a targeted backport if needed (customer on enterprise plan). :thumbsup:

kevin: will draft the patch today and drop a cc here when there's a test. expecting PR by EOD PST.

anya: also documenting in the support playbook: streaming through buffering proxies can cause chunk padding; add troubleshooting checklist and the three mitigations above.

alex: noted, closing loop here once PR and customer validation complete.
